summary: The statement and proof are correct. The simplex has the asserted integral vertices, is full-dimensional, and gives exactly the finite complete convex downset claimed. The positive and negative parts characterize distinct differences because A_j is a downset; the support formula, inclusion-exclusion formula, coefficient formula, and truncated recurrence all follow with the stated bounds and include zero and both orientations correctly. The multinomial weights enumerate every original twelve-dimensional center, including centers with zero coordinates. The origin, t=0 boundary, empty supports, and all-one center satisfy the formulas. The supplied integer program was executed: all 25 table rows, all 6720 permutation classes, the total counts, the products, the deficit, both outer-level sums, and both explicit-center comparisons were verified exactly. A separate implementation using support allocations and bounded-composition inclusion-exclusion independently reproduced every census row. Direct difference-set enumeration additionally agreed with both counting methods on 284 small and boundary instances. No mathematical error or gap was found, and no external source or predecessor fact is needed.
